subject: APAC marketplace usage mismatch — proposed reconciliation & collection steps
messages:
From: accounts@acme-corp.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Question about May marketplace charge (APAC)

Hi Marcus,

We've just received the AWS and Azure consolidated marketplace invoices for May and there's a material variance vs the consumption numbers you shared in the billing export. AWS shows a $24,350 charge tagged to 'redwood-inference' marketplace listings, while our internal metering indicates ~50% of that usage should be attributed to a partner-managed tenant that we pay directly.

Can you confirm the breakdown you see on your side and share the full per-tenant metering CSV and any rate card applied? I'm attaching the AWS invoice we received (Acme_Invoice_May2026.pdf). If we can't reconcile quickly we'll need to withhold the disputed portion on our next payment run.

Thanks,
Aisha Kim
Billing Manager | Acme Corp
accounts@acme-corp.com

Attachment: Acme_Invoice_May2026.pdf (PDF, 712KB)

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: accounts@acme-corp.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about May marketplace charge (APAC)

Hi Aisha — thanks for flagging this. We pulled the internal metering export and the APAC rate card; attaching both. At first glance the variance looks like two issues:

1) An attribution mismatch where ~40% of partner-tenant usage was routed through our hosted SKU for a 72-hour window (config drift during a canary).
2) A discounting/credit that AWS applied on their consolidated invoice which the line-item parser mis-assigned to a different account.

Action items I propose:
- I'll open a ticket with AWS Marketplace billing and request a line-item reallocation (cc-ing their billing alias).
- Marissa, can you produce a reconciled journal (redwood_metering_export_May2026.csv) showing tenant-level usage and applied unit prices?
- Sean, please prepare a short collection note that we can send Acme indicating the disputed amount and proposed payment schedule.

We should avoid payment hold if possible, but we need a clear remediation plan within 7 business days.

Marcus Lin
Senior Finance Ops | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_metering_export_May2026.csv (CSV), apac-rate-card-2026.pdf (PDF)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, accounts@acme-corp.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 08:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about May marketplace charge (APAC)

Hi all — attached is the tenant-level journal export. I added a reconciliation sheet with three tabs: 'Raw meter', 'Attribution adjustments', and 'Final ledger'.

Summary highlights:
- Line 1248–1263: the 72-hour canary generated ~9,800 extra tokens billed to the hosted SKU (estimated $9,600).
- AWS consolidated credit (invoice line C-45) was incorrectly applied against a cancelled offer ID on their side; we've asked them to reassign it.
- Net disputed amount: $8,900 (we propose Redwood absorbs $2,000 as a goodwill credit and request Acme pay $6,900).

Please review and let me know if you'd like me to convert the reconciliation to journal entries for accounting.

Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_metering_export_May2026.csv (CSV)

From: aws-marketplace-billing@amazon.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 05:41:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: reallocation of consolidated invoice credit (Acme Corp)

Hi Marissa / Marcus,

Thanks for the details and the meter export. We've researched invoice C-45 — it was issued as a consolidated account-level credit during our April batch but was tagged to the legacy offer ID due to a mapping issue in our ingestion pipeline. We will reissue the credit as a reversal and reapply it to the correct marketplace account within 5 business days.

Next steps from AWS:
- We will generate a corrected invoice and provide a line-item CSV showing the reassigned credit.
- You'll receive a support ticket number: AWS-615423.

Please confirm if you still need us to allocate usage to your partner-managed tenant (that requires a merchant-of-record reconciliation on Acme's side).

Regards,
Ravi Patel
AWS Marketplace Billing
aws-marketplace-billing@amazon.com

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: accounts@acme-corp.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about May marketplace charge (APAC) — proposed collection note

Hi Aisha — quick note from Redwood on the disputed portion. Per Marcus and Marissa's reconciliation we believe $8,900 of the $24,350 total is in dispute. Our proposal to keep cashflow moving:

1) Acme pays the undisputed balance of $15,450 by June 10.
2) Redwood and Acme will hold $6,900 in escrow while we wait for AWS to reissue the corrected line-item credit.
3) Redwood will cover a $2,000 goodwill credit immediately; if AWS reallocates the full $2,000 plus the remaining $4,900, we'll refund accordingly.

If that works, please reply 'Agreed' and we'll generate an invoice and escrow instructions (DocuSign link to follow).

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

From: accounts@acme-corp.com
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 16:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about May marketplace charge (APAC) — proposed collection note

Sean / Marcus / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear plan. We agree to the split payment and escrow approach: Acme will release $15,450 on our June 10 run and set aside $6,900 in a short-term hold. We appreciate Redwood's $2,000 goodwill credit.

Please send the DocuSign escrow instructions and the corrected journal once AWS publishes the reissued invoice (AWS-615423). We'll keep Treasury in the loop and expect the final settlement within 14 days of the corrected invoice.

Agreed,
Aisha Kim
Billing Manager | Acme Corp
accounts@acme-corp.com
